definitions.name: status lifecycle correlates gateway identities and distinguishes requested, selected and provider models
status distinguishes overlapping sessions and ignores discovery, counting and unauthenticated traffic
SSE errors remain observable after HTTP success and model confirmation with only a safe error category
status surfaces rejected request shapes and HTTP errors, and preserves fallback metadata

assertion_order_scope: Raw successful assertion order retained separately. Per-site and per-callback counts are exact; no scheduling or chunk partition equivalence is inferred.
network_scope: Actual synthetic loopback HTTP only; the original injected routing callbacks remain supplied mocks; no evaluator calls.
capture_semantics: Complete selected callbacks and five helper statements restored unchanged except successful assertion-result wrappers. Recording delegates actual HTTP and original return objects; no clone/drain, substituted verdict, timing threshold or source clock changes. Per-peer complete bodies preserve actual parser-delivered bytes; raw push chunks and chronological reads remain in raw observations. Provider request bodies remain unread by the original callbacks. Injected deterministic route latencies 42 and 33 remain unchanged; only measured first-response/total timings are projected. #24 keeps every emitted event in the independent recorder while its original statuses array is reset as written.
typed_observations: Headers inputs are enumerated into their complete normalized field map.
Route signal observation records actual AbortSignal type and aborted state; no serialized object identity is claimed. countTokens is recorded as a function capability only.
Individual response chunks remain base64, including intentionally split UTF-8. Only complete request bodies use UTF-8 after exact roundtrip validation.
